scope: desktop file drop and paste adapter: portable strict parsers plus Windows bounded HGLOBAL/OLE drop target, GTK3 text/uri-list drop destination and AppKit NSPasteboard drag destination

received_repairs: request_from_unicode_text bounds wcsnlen by GlobalSize()/sizeof(wchar_t) and refuses a buffer without a NUL inside it
request_from_file_group checks the header size and that cItems is covered by the real descriptor array before indexing fgd[]
request_from_hdrop validates the DROPFILES header, the pFiles offset and a wide or ANSI list that terminates inside the allocation before the shell parses it

the Windows target installs one transparent window procedure so WM_DESTROY revokes the OLE registration and WM_NCDESTROY restores it, removing the COM reference that survived a window destroyed before detach
malformed buffers are proven safe by tiny/unterminated/odd-length/lying-count/out-of-range HGLOBAL negatives plus an AddressSanitizer build and a live-target hook build
the wide FileGroupDescriptorW clipboard atom is registered from an explicit wide literal (CFSTR_FILEDESCRIPTORW is narrow in this SDK)

limits: One GitHub Actions runner per platform; no physical device and no interactive pointer drag.
Windows drops are delivered through the adapter entry OLE calls for IDropTarget::Drop with a real shell data object (SHCreateDataObject) and synthetic COM objects; no pointer-device drag is started.
AddressSanitizer runs with detect_leaks=0; persistent COM reclamation is proven by the hook build's live-target counter instead of a heap-leak report.
The clipboard normalises CF_UNICODETEXT, so the clipboard negative is structural (HDROP pFiles outside the allocation); unterminated and odd-length text negatives run on the IDataObject route.
GTK payloads travel through a real X11 clipboard under Xvfb and the installed drop destination; the drag gesture itself is not synthesised.
AppKit payloads travel through a real private NSPasteboard and an NSDraggingInfo double into the installed destination view; no NSWindow drag session is started.

previous_acceptance.note: Kept as the first acceptance; superseded for the repaired source because it could not observe the allocation bounds, the narrow clipboard atom or the COM reference left by a destroyed window.

rejected_runs.reason: guard also scanned the host example
GTK clipboard API and six portable fixtures
GTK main-context guard, cancel fixture and toolkit noise
probes clobbered their own target handles
MSYS mangled /fsanitize=address; narrow CFSTR_FILEDESCRIPTORW; const COM vtable
clipboard normalises unterminated text, so that negative was not deterministic

notes: Evidence was committed after the run with [skip ci]; the final HEAD adds only the two documentation files listed in documentation_only_delta.

The Windows report binds the release, hook and AddressSanitizer probe streams plus the portable sanitizer run and five stderr scans, so every memory-safety and lifecycle claim is inside the attested artifact.
Hook counters are compiled out of the installed binary; the installed package exports only the documented public API.
Host wiring, product acceptance and the shared-source re-verification remain with root.
